body.statement: Maximum directed indegree one versus two is a sharp worst-case computational frontier for pointwise numerical edge identification with feasible rational positive-definite covariance: \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_1\) has deterministic polynomial bit complexity with constructive certificates, whereas \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete even on depth-one directed graphs whose directed weak components are isolated vertices, single directed edges, or two-parent in-stars.  Equivalently, the hard family uses private roots, has maximum directed outdegree one, and has directed component size at most three.  At directed indegree zero there is no directed-edge query.
body.justification: The constructive fan-in-one trichotomy and the bounded-component fan-in-two completeness result meet at consecutive indegrees, yielding the exact worst-case structural boundary.
body.gap: No closest paper states an all-covariance bounded-directed-fan-in frontier for numerical edge fibers: existing low-fan-in results are generic, while prior numerical hardness uses an unbounded-fan-in storage sink even though it already preserves the complete fiber.
body.consumer: Graphical SEM software can use maximum directed indegree as a certified dispatch rule between exact specialized auditing and general real-algebraic methods, with the warning that the hard side persists on components of size three.
body.proof_tex:
By the established fan-in-one algorithm theorem, every promised instance of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_1\) is processed in deterministic polynomial bit complexity.  Its case \(\mathrm{(i)}\) returns a singleton attainable set and is therefore a YES instance by the promise-problem definition.  In case \(\mathrm{(ii)}\), the two feasible matrices have unequal queried coordinates, and in case \(\mathrm{(iii)}\), the feasible curve has a nonconstant queried coordinate; either case exhibits two elements of \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)\) and is therefore a NO instance.  The same theorem supplies the unique rational value or the promised componentwise-quadratic witness or curve certificate, so this is a constructive decision procedure, not merely a membership bound.

The fan-in-two completeness theorem proves that \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete under the same rational positive-definite feasibility promise.  Its hardness family is more restricted than the fan-in-two class: the directed subgraph has depth one and each of its weak components is an isolated vertex, a single directed edge, or a two-parent in-star.  Equivalently for that family, roots are private, the maximum directed outdegree is one, and every directed component has at most three vertices.  Thus the hard side is already present immediately at the next possible positive fan-in.

If the maximum directed indegree is zero, then \(D=\varnothing\): any edge \((u,v)\in D\) would give \(v\) directed indegree at least one.  Since a numerical edge query requires \(e\in D\), no such query exists at fan-in zero.  The tractable result at one, the restricted hardness result at two, and this zero-fan-in observation prove the stated sharp worst-case frontier while preserving all constructive certificate claims on the tractable side.
